## 2026-07-24 — Quiz engine gains a `map-move` result style; Scrum-Master-in-an-AI-world quiz replaces the AI-failure-modes quiz

**Why.** The next lead-magnet quiz ("Where is the Scrum Master role going in an
AI world?", concept C in the handoff) needed a fundamentally different result:
not a single "you scored X, you're a Y" band, but a per-answer *map* (work
getting more valuable vs. work slipping away) plus one recommended *move*. The
engine only did band results. Rather than hardcode the new logic into a page, we
generalized the engine into a pluggable result-strategy so more quiz types can
follow.

**What we did.**
- **Engine:** added a `resultStyle: 'band' | 'map-move'` frontmatter field
  (defaults to `band`, so nothing changes for band quizzes). Options gained an
  optional `bucket` (`gaining` / `mixed` / `slipping` / `context`) and per-answer
  sentences (`mapSentence`, `reclaimSentence`, `redirectSentence`). A new
  `mapMove` frontmatter block holds the move-selection priorities plus all the
  surrounding copy. New pure module `map-move.ts` (`computeMapMove`,
  `buildMapMoveQuery`, `parseMapMoveResponses`) and a `MapMoveResults.astro`
  component. `sectionLevels` / `overallLevels` became optional so map-move quizzes
  can omit them. The engine stays APR-agnostic: all wording lives in frontmatter.
- **The move.** Reclaim target = highest-priority *slipping* answer
  (Q3 admin > Q1 > Q2); redirect target = highest-priority weak coaching/systemic
  answer (Q4 > Q7 > Q8 > Q5 > Q6). The two never collide. If nothing is slipping,
  the result shows the "well-positioned" fallback instead of a move. A light
  descriptive framing line (never an archetype) comes from the gaining/slipping
  ratio. The `context` ("d") answers — part-time role, no PO to coach, hands-on in
  the build — are named honestly but **never** scored as gaps.
- **Results page** now dispatches on `resultStyle`. The stepper builds the band
  query or the map-move `?a=` query accordingly. The landing page's previously
  hardcoded AI-quiz copy (hero button, "Twelve questions" proof bullets, capture
  footnote, correctness highlighting) moved to frontmatter fields so each quiz
  supplies its own.
- **Content + routing.** New quiz at `src/content/quizzes/scrum-master-ai/`,
  tagged `sm-role-ai`. The old `ai-failure-modes` quiz was removed (wholesale
  replacement); `/quiz/ai-failure-modes/` now 301s to `/quiz/scrum-master-ai/`,
  and the two existing quiz redirects (`/scrum-pain-quiz/`, `/agile-checkup/`)
  were repointed to the new slug.
- **Open item:** the results-page course CTA (heading/body/button) is a
  placeholder pointing at `/contact-us/` pending the final "Pragmatic AI for Agile
  Teams" course name + URL.

## 2026-07-23 — CSM and CSD workbooks migrated to hosted `/materials/` (following CSPO)

Done. The engine now supports a pluggable result strategy, and Quiz C is built on it. Everything type-checks clean (0 errors/warnings/hints) and the production build passes. I stopped at diff-ready, no commit.

## What changed

**Engine generalization (`src/lib/quiz-engine/`)** — added a `resultStyle: 'band' | 'map-move'` field (defaults to `band`, so nothing changes for band quizzes):
- `schema.ts` / `types.ts` — options gained `bucket` (`gaining`/`mixed`/`slipping`/`context`) + per-answer sentences; new `mapMove` config block; `sectionLevels`/`overallLevels` now optional.
- `map-move.ts` (new) — pure `computeMapMove` (classify + pick the one reclaim/redirect move), `buildMapMoveQuery`/`parseMapMoveResponses`.
- `MapMoveResults.astro` (new) — renders the two-column map + move + context notes + CTA, all from frontmatter.
- `QuizStepper.tsx` builds the right query per style; `results.astro` dispatches on `resultStyle`. The old `ai-failure-modes` band quiz would still work unchanged.

**Content + routing** — new quiz at `src/content/quizzes/scrum-master-ai/`, tagged `sm-role-ai`. Old quiz removed; `/quiz/ai-failure-modes/` 301s to the new slug and the two existing quiz redirects were repointed. Landing-page copy that was hardcoded for the AI quiz (hero button, "Twelve questions" bullets, footnote, correctness highlighting) moved to frontmatter.

**Verified:** the move logic against the draft's two worked examples — admin-heavy → reclaim Q3 + redirect Q4, framing "slipping"; all-strong → well-positioned; and the part-time **"d" answers land in context, never counted as slipping** (§7). The SSR results page is covered by `astro check` + build bundling (I couldn't curl it — the sandbox blocks localhost).

## Two things I need / flagged for you

1. **Course CTA — I need the name + URL.** You chose "I'll give you the name + URL." Right now the results-page CTA is a clearly-marked placeholder: heading "Pragmatic AI for Agile Teams", button → `/contact-us/` (see the `# PLACEHOLDER` comment in the quiz frontmatter). Give me the final name and link and I'll drop them in.

2. **Review the "context" (d-answer) sentences.** The draft's reviewed copy (§3) didn't include per-question copy for the "d" constraint answers, so I **authored those eight sentences** to satisfy §7 (name the constraint, don't score it). They're my draft in your voice — worth a read. The map/slipping/gaining sentences and all other copy are lifted from your reviewed §3.

Minor note: the engine's capture screen still reads "Where should we send your results?" (your draft said "Where should I send your result?"). Left as the engine default since it's shared with band quizzes; easy to parametrize if you want the exact wording.

`.claude/settings.local.json` also shows as modified — that's incidental (permission-prompt bookkeeping from this session), not part of the feature.

1. **Email statement on the quiz home page** — added a line right under the hero CTA: *"Free. To see your results, you'll add your email at the end."* (`src/pages/quiz/[slug].astro`).

**What happened:** earlier I launched `astro dev` in the background to smoke-test, then ran `npm run build` twice against the same project. The build shares Vite's cache/runtime with the running dev daemon, which closed its module runner out from under the live server, producing that repeating "Vite module runner has been closed" error. It was the leftover test server, not your code.

To get a clean dev server back, just run:

```
npm run dev
```

It'll start fresh with a healthy Vite runtime. (I've now stopped starting background dev servers — the build verification I did is sufficient and doesn't collide with a server you're running.)
